title: Scaling a Circle into an Ellipse
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Put the equation 9x^2 + 25y^2 = 225 into standard form, identify its semi-axes, and explain how it can be obtained by scaling the unit circle x^2 + y^2 = 1.
finalAnswer: \frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1; \quad a = 5, \ b = 3; \quad \text{Scaled by 5 horizontally and 3 vertically}

steps.title: Convert to Standard Form
steps.explanation: Divide both sides of the equation by 225 to achieve the standard normalized form where the right-hand constant equals 1.
steps.why: Standard form for an ellipse centered at the origin requires a unit right-hand side.

steps.title: Identify Semi-Axes Lengths
steps.explanation: The semi-major axis along the x-axis has length a = 5, and the semi-minor axis along the y-axis has length b = 3. The x-intercepts are (+-5, 0) and y-intercepts are (0, +-3).
steps.why: The denominators in standard form represent the squares of the semi-axes.

steps.title: Explain the Transformation from the Unit Circle
steps.explanation: Starting from the unit circle X^2 + Y^2 = 1, substituting X = x/5 stretches the circle horizontally by a factor of 5, and substituting Y = y/3 stretches it vertically by a factor of 3, generating the ellipse.
steps.why: Replacing coordinate variables with scaled fractions expands the geometry along the corresponding coordinate axes.
